whatItIs.text: A ripe red jalapeño, smoke-dried for days until it shrivels like a raisin — heat wrapped in woodsmoke, most often sold stewed in adobo sauce.

historyNote.text: The name is Nahuatl chīlpoctli, 'smoked chili': Mesoamericans, including the Aztecs, preserved chillies by smoke-drying long before the technique reached any European kitchen. Ten pounds of jalapeños make one pound of chipotle.

howToChoose.text: In adobo tins, choose brands listing chillies before thickeners; dried moritas are darker and milder-fruited, mecos smokier and more traditional.

storage.text: Refrigerate the opened tin; freeze spoonfuls on a tray.

useItUp.text: Blitz the whole tin into a smoky marinade or mayo; one chipotle with a spoon of its sauce transforms a pot of beans or a burger.

substitutions.note: smoke and heat without the fruit
